# South Africa

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.51, by age as below | DHS 2016, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −0.54 | DHS 2016, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | −1.77 | census 2007, 45q15 |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.28 | −0.60 | −0.30 | −0.18 | −0.41 | −0.90 | −1.49 |

**Adult and child mortality gradient by age** (`mort_gradient`; ages 15–59: the 45q15 gradient above plus the pooled offset for each band ([age pattern](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)); ages 5–14 use the 15–29 value; ages 60–74 fall in a straight line from the 45–59 value to 0 at age 75; ages 75 and above, and OG-Core's final age, use 0):

| 1–4 | 5–14 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | 75+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pending | −2.14 | −2.14 | −1.92 | −1.58 | −1.58 at 60, falling to 0 at 75 | 0 |

Ages 1–4 await a decision on the method (the child-mortality gradient at ages 1–4; [ROADMAP](../../ROADMAP.md) item A3). Infant mortality (age 0) is `infmort_gradient`, above.

## Estimates

### Household surveys

Latest Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) or Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown, for each indicator ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | DHS 2016 | 3.1 | 2.9 | 2.7 | 2.3 | 2.1 | 1.48 | −0.51 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 2016 | 54 | 44 | 46 | 27 | 40 | 1.35 | −0.54 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 2016 | 67 | 52 | 51 | 34 | 41 | 1.63 | −0.70 |

### Adult mortality from household-death records

Wealth gradients in 45q15 and in age-specific death rates, both sexes ([`adult_mortality_gradients.csv`](../../data/adult_mortality_gradients.csv); [methods](../methods/adult-mortality.md); estimates by sex in the [full table](../tables/adult_mortality.md)). Blank cells: too few deaths to publish.

| Source | 45q15 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | Wealth groups | Deaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Census 2001 | −1.16 | −1.04 | −1.45 | −0.98 | −0.34 | 5 | 20,193 |
| Census 2007 | −1.77 | −1.63 | −2.00 | −1.58 | −0.69 | 5 | 9,467 |

Source: IPUMS International (Ruggles et al., doi:10.18128/D020.V7.7); original data: Statistics South Africa.

## Notes

- Adult-mortality estimates are published for the 2001 and 2007 censuses; 2007 is the latest and is used for `mort_gradient`. In 2007 the death records match the deaths households report in every wealth group. The 2001 census does not record the number of deaths per household, so that check could not be made.
- The 2011 census is not published. Only about 9 percent of its death records can be linked to a household, and the linked share is lower in wealthier households: compared with the deaths households report, it falls by 15–20 percent from the lowest to the highest wealth group. This would make the gradient too steep by about 0.3.
- The 2016 DHS child-mortality rates by quintile are based on few deaths and are not monotonic in the upper quintiles; the gradient is usable, the individual quintile rates less so.
